attribution.author: Paul McWhorter
attribution.note: Lesson curriculum based on Paul McWhorter's Arduino tutorial series at toptechboy.com. Please support his free educational work on Patreon.

tracks.name: Arduino Electronics
tracks.blurb: Build real circuits and write the C++ that drives them — LEDs, sensors, servos, motors, and displays.

tracks.name: Build on Your Computer
tracks.blurb: Leave the sandbox: set up your own machine. The command line, git, compilers, and running real projects — typed, not clicked.

tracks.name: Python & Raspberry Pi
tracks.blurb: Carry your electronics instincts into Python — same circuits, new language, on a Raspberry Pi.

tracks.name: AI & Machine Learning
tracks.blurb: From sensors to smarts: teach your projects to see, classify, and decide.

lessons.title: Digital Output — LED Blink
lessons.description: Control a digital pin and blink an LED using pinMode() and digitalWrite(). Build the circuit: pin 13 → resistor → LED → GND.
lessons.source: Paul McWhorter, Arduino Tutorials 1–2 — toptechboy.com

circuit.notes: Wire pin 13 to one side of the resistor, the other side to the LED anode (A), and the LED cathode (C) to GND.

lessons.title: Analog Input — Potentiometer
lessons.description: Read a potentiometer, map its value, and print to the serial monitor. Wire the pot: VCC→5V, GND→GND, SIG→A0.
lessons.source: Paul McWhorter, Arduino Tutorial 10 — toptechboy.com

circuit.notes: The wiper (SIG) picks off a voltage between 0V and 5V. Wire it to analog pin A0.

lessons.title: Serial Monitor — Talking to Your Arduino
lessons.description: Use Serial.begin(), Serial.print(), and Serial.println() to send readable data to your computer. No external circuit needed.
lessons.source: Paul McWhorter, Arduino serial tutorials — toptechboy.com

circuit.notes: No external parts — the serial monitor communicates over the USB cable.

lessons.title: Variables — Making Code Adjustable
lessons.description: Replace magic numbers with named int variables so one edit changes the whole sketch. Same LED circuit as Lesson 1.
lessons.source: Paul McWhorter, Arduino Tutorial 4 (Variables) — toptechboy.com

circuit.notes: Rebuild the Lesson 1 circuit: pin → resistor → LED anode, cathode → GND.

lessons.title: Conditionals — Making Decisions
lessons.description: Use if/else to switch the LED based on the potentiometer: turn it past halfway and the light comes on.
lessons.source: Paul McWhorter, Arduino if-statement tutorials — toptechboy.com

circuit.notes: Two sub-circuits: the pot (VCC/GND/SIG→A0) for input, and pin 13 → resistor → LED → GND for output.

lessons.title: Digital Input — Pushbutton
lessons.description: Read a pushbutton with INPUT_PULLUP and light the LED while it's held. Remember: with a pullup, pressed reads LOW.
lessons.source: Paul McWhorter, Arduino button tutorials — toptechboy.com

circuit.notes: Button between pin 2 and GND (INPUT_PULLUP handles the rest internally). LED circuit on pin 13 as usual.

lessons.title: Debouncing — Clean Button Presses
lessons.description: Metal contacts bounce. Use millis() to ignore changes for 50ms so one press counts exactly once — toggle the LED per press.
lessons.source: Paul McWhorter, Arduino debounce tutorials — toptechboy.com

circuit.notes: Same wiring as Lesson 6: button on pin 2 to GND, LED circuit on pin 13.

lessons.title: Light Sensor — Photoresistor
lessons.description: Read the light level with a photoresistor module and print it to the serial monitor. Cover the sensor and watch the numbers fall.
lessons.source: Paul McWhorter, Arduino photoresistor tutorials — toptechboy.com

circuit.notes: Module wiring: VCC→5V, GND→GND, AO→A0. The AO voltage rises with brightness.

lessons.title: Night Light — Light + LED
lessons.description: Combine sensing and output: when it gets dark, the LED turns on automatically — a real night light.
lessons.source: Paul McWhorter, Arduino light-meter tutorials — toptechboy.com

circuit.notes: Photoresistor module AO→A0, plus the LED circuit on pin 13.

lessons.title: Temperature — NTC Thermistor
lessons.description: Read temperature with an NTC thermistor module and print approximate °C using map().
lessons.source: Paul McWhorter, Arduino thermistor tutorials — toptechboy.com

circuit.notes: Module wiring: VCC→5V, GND→GND, OUT→A0.

lessons.title: Ultrasonic Distance — HC-SR04
lessons.description: Measure distance like a bat: ping with TRIG, time the echo with pulseIn(), and convert microseconds to centimeters.
lessons.source: Paul McWhorter, Arduino HC-SR04 tutorials — toptechboy.com

circuit.notes: Wiring: VCC→5V, GND→GND, TRIG→pin 9, ECHO→pin 10.

lessons.title: Distance Alarm — Sonar + LED
lessons.description: The capstone: when something comes closer than 20cm, the warning LED lights — a parking sensor.
lessons.source: Paul McWhorter, Arduino distance-alarm tutorials — toptechboy.com

circuit.notes: HC-SR04 wiring (TRIG→9, ECHO→10) plus the LED circuit on pin 13.

lessons.title: PWM — Dimming an LED
lessons.description: analogWrite() pulses a pin faster than the eye can see — the duty cycle becomes brightness. Fade the LED up and down with for loops.
lessons.source: Paul McWhorter, Arduino analogWrite/PWM tutorials — toptechboy.com

circuit.notes: Same LED circuit, but on a PWM pin: pin 9 (~) → resistor → LED anode, cathode → GND.

lessons.title: RGB LED — Mixing Colors
lessons.description: Three PWM channels, 16.7 million colors. Drive the red, green, and blue legs with analogWrite() and mix your own color.
lessons.source: Paul McWhorter, Arduino RGB LED tutorials — toptechboy.com

circuit.notes: COM (longest leg) → GND. R leg → pin 9, G leg → pin 10, B leg → pin 11 (all PWM ~). Real builds put a 220Ω on each leg.

lessons.title: Servo — Sweep
lessons.description: A servo moves to the exact angle you command. Include the Servo library, attach pin 9, and sweep the horn from 0° to 180° and back.
lessons.source: Paul McWhorter, Arduino servo tutorials — toptechboy.com

circuit.notes: Servo wiring: GND → GND, V+ → 5V, PWM (signal) → pin 9.

lessons.title: Servo + Potentiometer — Steering
lessons.description: Close the loop with your own hand: map the pot's 0–1023 onto 0–180° and the servo horn follows the knob.
lessons.source: Paul McWhorter, Arduino servo knob tutorials — toptechboy.com

circuit.notes: Servo: GND→GND, V+→5V, PWM→pin 9. Pot: VCC→5V, GND→GND, SIG→A0.

lessons.title: DC Motor — Fan Speed
lessons.description: PWM sets the motor's average voltage, and average voltage is speed. The pot becomes a fan-speed dial.
lessons.source: Paul McWhorter, Arduino DC motor tutorials — toptechboy.com

circuit.notes: Motor: terminal 1 → pin 9 (~), terminal 2 → GND. Pot: VCC→5V, GND→GND, SIG→A0. (Real builds add a transistor driver + flyback diode.)

lessons.title: LCD — Hello, World!
lessons.description: Ten wires and your project can talk. Wire the 16×2 display and print text plus a live seconds counter.
lessons.source: Paul McWhorter, Arduino LCD tutorials — toptechboy.com

circuit.notes: Power: VSS→GND, VDD→5V, V0→GND, RW→GND, A→5V, K→GND. Signals: RS→12, E→11, D4→5, D5→4, D6→3, D7→2.

lessons.title: LCD Thermometer
lessons.description: Combine the temp sensor with the display: a self-contained instrument that shows °C with no computer attached.
lessons.source: Paul McWhorter, Arduino LCD + sensor tutorials — toptechboy.com

circuit.notes: LCD wired as in Lesson 18 (RS→12, E→11, D4→5, D5→4, D6→3, D7→2). Temp sensor: VCC→5V, GND→GND, OUT→A0.

lessons.title: Capstone — Parking Radar
lessons.description: Everything at once: sonar measures distance, the LCD reports it, and the RGB LED glows green → amber → red as you get close.
lessons.source: Paul McWhorter, Arduino capstone-style projects — toptechboy.com

circuit.notes: Sonar: TRIG→8, ECHO→10. LCD: RS→12, E→11, D4→7, D5→6, D6→4, D7→2. RGB: R leg→3, G leg→5, COM→GND.
